claims.statement: The Commission lists risk management, data quality, activity logging, detailed documentation, human oversight, robustness, cybersecurity, and accuracy among obligations for high-risk AI systems before market placement.
Official guidance says certain deployers must perform a fundamental-rights impact assessment, while deployers generally must monitor use, act on risks or incidents, and assign human oversight.
The Commission's current timeline says rules for specified high-risk areas apply from 2 December 2027 and product-integrated high-risk systems from 2 August 2028.

contrary_evidence: The Commission says the vast majority of AI systems are minimal or no risk, so a broad horizontal target would have weak mandatory demand.
Current high-risk application dates are in 2027-2028, delaying urgency and leaving room for further implementation changes.
Draft classification guidance is not legally binding and was still undergoing consultation, so product rules cannot be treated as settled legal advice.

economics.acquisition_route: Select one vertical after 20-30 interviews, run paid evidence-mapping pilots with an AI/privacy advisor, and turn the common model into integrations
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-8 year scenario: 80 providers averaging 80,000 PLN annual revenue yields 6.4m PLN; at 30% EBITDA, 4x, and 70% ownership, equity value is about 5.38m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 17-23 hours weekly, with external legal and sector assurance input at fixed milestones
economics.gross_margin_basis: Evidence orchestration and reusable vertical schemas are software; bespoke legal classification, bias studies, and assurance are partner-delivered services
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: reducing enterprise diligence cycles and repeated evidence assembly could justify 50,000-120,000 PLN annually, but willingness before enforcement must be tested
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 20,000-60,000 PLN implementation and 36,000-120,000 PLN annual subscription per provider based on systems and deployments
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every data, model, intended-purpose, oversight, deployment, and incident change extends the same audit trail

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal model/data/control lineage plus vertical evaluation and incident patterns, with customer-confidential data isolated
fingerprint.customer: EU SME providers of AI systems in one selected high-risk vertical, initially HR, education, or credit software rather than general-purpose model labs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: AI assurance firms, privacy advisors, sector software associations, and downloadable vertical evidence schemas that reveal readiness gaps
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Classification decision log, data/evaluation lineage, control assignments, trace logging, technical-document export, and change gate; hypothesis 20,000-60,000 PLN setup plus 3,000-10,000 PLN monthly
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: CTO, risk, or compliance leader pays onboarding and an annual license per governed system, with optional validation-study modules
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Classification review, new model release, material data/model change, enterprise procurement review, authority request, or serious incident

founder_fit: Direct match for data science, model evaluation, data lineage, and AI-assisted workflow building
Vertical product can be developed part-time and sold through specialist partners
Does not require the founder to become an influencer or make medical decisions
Quantitative evaluation and reproducible evidence match the founder's work style
risks: AI Act timelines and guidance are still evolving, creating product and demand-timing risk
Incorrect classification or assurance language could be relied on as legal advice
Cloud and model-platform incumbents may add governance and logging features
Sensitive training and decision data create significant privacy and security duties

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical AI-governance system of record licensed per governed model/system and deployment
structure.control_point: The lifecycle approval record linking high-risk classification, evidence, human oversight, and release authorization for each system version
structure.critical_dependency: Correct classification and intended-purpose scoping plus trustworthy access to training/evaluation data, logs, model changes, and accountable human owners

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: create an evidence graph and approval workflow for smaller providers of potentially high-risk AI used in employment, education, credit, insurance, or regulated products. It would bind a system's intended purpose and classification decision to dataset lineage, evaluation slices, human-oversight controls, logs, technical documentation, change approvals, and post-market incidents. The wedge is a deterministic release packet for one vertical, such as Polish HR software vendors, with optional deployer evidence exports. The control point is the internal decision to release or materially change a system, while an accumulating lineage graph raises switching costs and makes audits less episodic.
title: High-Risk AI Lifecycle Evidence Graph
uncertainties: Best first vertical and number of genuinely high-risk SME providers in Poland/EU
Whether providers buy before applicable dates or wait for customer mandates
Minimum technical integrations needed to be a release gate rather than a document repository
How conformity and assurance standards settle for each vertical
